# ICML Review

## Summary

Mini Artichokes is an asymmetric selective ensemble: D1 is the preassigned base, and only all-valid conflicts where D2 and D3 agree against D1 are sent to a judge that must choose an existing anonymous candidate. [ev_p003_b005 · p.3] [ev_p003_b006 · p.3] [ev_p003_b013 · p.3] [ev_p003_b015 · p.3] Across two disjoint, unchanged-policy 1,000-question MMLU-Pro cohorts, OJ3 scored 60.70% versus D1's 59.35%, a 1.35-point gain with 33 rescues, 6 harms, one-sided exact p=7.15e-6, and bootstrap interval of +0.75 to +1.95 points. [ev_p004_b002 · p.4] [ev_p004_b007 · p.4] [ev_p005_b012 · p.5] [ev_p014_b014 · p.14] OJ3 did not significantly outperform majority voting or the matched generic judge, required 3.53 times D1's tokens, and reversed direction on the Korean legal reserve; the evidence therefore supports only a benchmark-specific advantage over direct inference. [ev_p005_b015 · p.5] [ev_p006_b009 · p.6] [ev_p006_b018 · p.6] [ev_p006_b022 · p.6]

## Strengths

- The matched generic-judge arm is a strong input-level control: it shares conflicts, anonymous candidates, rotation, model settings, call count, and fallback, while OJ3 adds the support treatment. [ev_p003_b013 · p.3] [ev_p003_b016 · p.3] [ev_p012_b011 · p.12]
- The evaluation uses deterministic disjoint sampling, an unchanged replication, full-denominator scoring, and explicit two-look and fixed-sequence controls. [ev_p004_b002 · p.4] [ev_p004_b007 · p.4] [ev_p004_b008 · p.4] [ev_p004_b010 · p.4] [ev_p004_b016 · p.4]
- The presentation carefully distinguishes the supported improvement over D1 from the nonsignificant comparisons with SC3 and GJ3 and avoids claiming universal transfer. [ev_p001_b005 · p.1] [ev_p005_b015 · p.5] [ev_p008_b004 · p.8]
- The paper reports extensive reproducibility material, including frozen prompts, artifact hashes, outputs, scoring scripts, and per-call receipt hashes. [ev_p008_b006 · p.8] [ev_p010_b017 · p.10] [ev_p012_b006 · p.12] [ev_p016_b003 · p.16]

## Weaknesses

- The item-level paired tests and bootstrap condition on one realized whole-file execution per arm and do not establish full-pipeline repeatability across sessions, despite an extreme preserved D2 failure. [ev_p004_b004 · p.4] [ev_p004_b005 · p.4] [ev_p007_b011 · p.7] [ev_p013_b011 · p.13] [ev_p013_b031 · p.13]
- The stated SC3 invariant is not implied by the definitions: when D1 is invalid but valid D2 and D3 agree, the conflict indicator is zero while SC3's majority rule returns their answer. [ev_p003_b006 · p.3] [ev_p003_b010 · p.3] [ev_p012_b013 · p.12] [ev_p012_b014 · p.12] [ev_p013_b026 · p.13] [ev_p013_b029 · p.13]
- The support-aware method has no statistically established advantage over the strong multi-call controls, while its significant comparison is against the substantially cheaper direct baseline. [ev_p006_b009 · p.6] [ev_p006_b022 · p.6] [ev_p014_b015 · p.14] [ev_p014_b016 · p.14]
- Generality is weakly supported: confirmation uses one model and benchmark, and the legal reversal does not isolate underdetermination from simultaneous changes in domain, task, and label structure. [ev_p003_b021 · p.3] [ev_p004_b019 · p.4] [ev_p006_b018 · p.6] [ev_p007_b004 · p.7] [ev_p007_b010 · p.7]
- Methodological novelty is modest because the contribution is chiefly a fixed asymmetric operating rule combining established repeated sampling, selective ensembling, and LLM candidate judgment. [ev_p002_b010 · p.2] [ev_p002_b012 · p.2] [ev_p002_b014 · p.2] [ev_p003_b013 · p.3]

## Questions for Authors

1. Can the authors repeat the complete D1–D3 and judge pipeline across independently initialized whole-file executions and report uncertainty that captures between-session variability? [ev_p004_b004 · p.4] [ev_p004_b005 · p.4] [ev_p007_b011 · p.7] [ev_p013_b011 · p.13] [ev_p013_b031 · p.13]
   Assessment change: Stable effects under repeated full-pipeline executions and session-level inference could raise the soundness assessment and improve the acceptance case; substantial run-to-run variation would weaken confidence in the headline effect.
2. How many rows had invalid D1 with valid, agreeing D2 and D3, and does the implementation gate SC3 on all-three validity despite the stated majority rule? [ev_p003_b006 · p.3] [ev_p003_b010 · p.3] [ev_p012_b013 · p.12] [ev_p012_b014 · p.12] [ev_p013_b026 · p.13] [ev_p013_b029 · p.13]
   Assessment change: Showing that no rows are affected, or providing corrected comparisons with unchanged conclusions, could resolve a major soundness concern; materially changed results would weaken the acceptance case.
3. Can the support annotation be evaluated with replicated or crossed judge sessions so that its effect is separated from whole-file session variation? [ev_p005_b021 · p.5] [ev_p007_b011 · p.7] [ev_p007_b013 · p.7] [ev_p012_b011 · p.12] [ev_p014_b016 · p.14]
   Assessment change: A powered, replicated OJ3-over-GJ3 effect would raise the soundness, significance, and originality assessments; a null result would confirm that the support annotation itself remains unestablished.
4. Does the policy retain an advantage on another model and determinate-answer benchmark, and what monetary, latency, or application-utility threshold makes the additional inference worthwhile? [ev_p005_b015 · p.5] [ev_p006_b009 · p.6] [ev_p006_b018 · p.6] [ev_p007_b008 · p.7] [ev_p007_b010 · p.7]
   Assessment change: A repeatable gain across another model and determinate-answer benchmark, with favorable latency and utility, could raise significance and improve the acceptance assessment; failure would reinforce the current narrow-scope conclusion.
5. Can the authors replace the host-specific path and document the legal reserve's source, reuse authority or license, de-identification procedure, residual re-identification risk, and reconstructible construction process? [ev_p004_b019 · p.4] [ev_p007_b018 · p.7] [ev_p007_b015 · p.7] [ev_p011_b024 · p.11] [ev_p016_b018 · p.16] [ev_p016_b022 · p.16]
   Assessment change: Complete documentation and redaction could resolve the identified data-governance and anonymity concerns and improve the acceptance assessment; unresolved gaps would sustain the ethical and reproducibility concerns.

## Limitations

Confirmation covers one model, one runtime, and one multiple-choice benchmark; the benchmark may also overlap model training data. [ev_p007_b010 · p.7] The whole-file regime permits context and cache effects and is not equivalent to independent per-question inference; the anomalous first-cohort D2 session demonstrates substantial session-level instability. [ev_p004_b005 · p.4] [ev_p007_b011 · p.7] [ev_p013_b031 · p.13] All semantic arms use the same model family, and only 68 of 2,000 questions triggered arbitration, leaving correlated-error behavior and the support treatment estimate poorly characterized. [ev_p007_b012 · p.7] [ev_p007_b013 · p.7] The 1.35-point gain over D1 required 3.53 times its tokens, while monetary cost and application-specific utility were not established. [ev_p006_b009 · p.6] [ev_p007_b008 · p.7] [ev_p007_b014 · p.7] The legal reserve is a narrow civil/tax outcome task and lacks sufficient supplied provenance and construction detail for independent reconstruction or broad legal conclusions. [ev_p004_b019 · p.4] [ev_p007_b015 · p.7] [ev_p016_b018 · p.16] [ev_p016_b022 · p.16]

## Overall Recommendation

3/6

## Confidence

5/5

## Ethical Concerns

Verified ethical concerns: The supplied blocks describe the Korean legal reserve as containing partial fact patterns from de-identified legal case records, but do not state the records' source, reuse authority or license, de-identification procedure, or residual re-identification-risk assessment. The supplement discloses the absolute host-specific path `/home/pineapple/.codex-new-account`, which creates a potential anonymity/linkage risk; the supplied evidence does not establish attribution to any author, institution, or externally searchable account.
